svg.title: Policy repair harness: explicit adapters, development evidence, and independent held-out evaluation
svg.desc: A pretrained VLA, WAM, or other learned policy and a simulator/task enter through explicit policy and benchmark adapters. The policy adapter declares streams, hooks, action semantics, capabilities, and edit scopes; the benchmark supplies layouts, rollouts, recordings, and outcomes. Adapter implementation and preflight are required; unsupported tools are omitted. During budgeted development, an LLM in Codex CLI exchanges MCP tool calls and evidence with a laboratory. The FULL condition provides both arbitrary Python using Lab, NumPy, and PyTorch and curated tools for matched controls, activation analysis, causal interventions, attribution, and saved-edit recipes. The laboratory and simulation policy worker load separate model instances. Saved tensor edits bridge them, and recorded observations, actions, model inputs, noise, hooks, and outcomes return as evidence. The agent journals falsifiable hypotheses, parent relationships, immutable candidate snapshots, and full-cohort validation repeats. Diagnostic screens and activation interventions are not final submissions. Selection retains the best eligible development improvement, or the base policy. The default controller remains sequential flush-only. Optional fork-flush starts four isolated fresh workspaces in sequential waves, selects the best validated lineage, and resumes the winner's same conversation for exploitation, repeating at aggregate 33 and 66 percent development-episode boundaries; losing branches count toward the budget. Joint eight-direction portfolios and balanced six-of-ten robot-metric views reuse RSI components, not its full treatment. There is no semantic deduplication, execute-all portfolio, or stall monitor. Fork-and-Flush helpers are an independent MIT implementation plus the paper algorithm, not author code. The prototype submits weight edits, not gradient-based fitting or LoRA; diagnostic gradients and closed-form fits are allowed. Merging and retrieval are future work. After selection, weights are frozen and an independent evaluator compares base and edited policies on paired held-out layouts, with no held-out feedback to the agent. Native-pipeline and side-effect checks are additional validation, not universal guarantees. Solid arrows indicate data or artifacts; dashed arrows indicate control. This is a harness diagram, not evidence of new scientific results.
svg.text: Task execution and scoring stay benchmark-specific
Explicit adapters + preflight required · unsupported tools omitted · not universal zero-code compatibility

Select validated lineage → resume winner’s same conversation
Repeat at 33% / 66% aggregate dev episodes · losing branches count
Default: sequential flush-only · weight edits, not gradient fitting / LoRA
03 / HELD OUT · OUTSIDE THE AGENT LOOP
Paired base vs. frozen edit · held-out layouts
No held-out feedback to the agent
